record.original_question: Let the function f where ∞ X f (z) = 1 + an z n , |z| ≤ 1, n=1 be a Bloch function with positive PN real part in D. Determine the rate of growth (as N → ∞) of the sequence 2 n=1 |an | . (F. Holland)

evidence.quote: Let the function f where ∞ X f (z) = 1 + an z n , |z| ≤ 1, n=1 be a Bloch function with positive PN real part in D. Determine the rate of growth (as N → ∞) of the sequence 2 n=1 |an | . (F. Holland)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc. An analytic function $g:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ is called a Bloch function if
$$\|g\|_{\mathcal{B}}:=\sup_{z\in\mathbb{D}}(1-|z|^2)|g'(z)|<\infty.$$
Let
$$f(z)=1+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n z^n,\qquad z\in\mathbb{D},$$
be analytic in $\mathbb{D}$, and assume that:
(i) $f$ is a Bloch function, and
(ii) $\operatorname{Re} f(z)>0$ for every $z\in\mathbb{D}$.

Determine the exact rate of growth, as $N\to\infty$, of the partial sums
$$S_N=\sum_{n=1}^{N}|a_n|^2.$$
That is, find a function $\varphi(N)$ such that $S_N \asymp \varphi(N)$ (or otherwise sharply describe the asymptotic behaviour of $S_N$) for all such $f$, and identify the extremal behaviour.
artifact.category_tag: Bloch functions in the unit disc
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search for the growth rate of $\sum_{n=1}^N |a_n|^2$ for Bloch functions with positive real part (a problem attributed to F. Holland) did not surface a definitive resolution. No published result was found that establishes the exact asymptotic rate, so the current status is unclear from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Bloch Functions: The Basic Theory
status_evidence.snippet: General reference on Bloch functions and their Taylor coefficients in the unit disc.
status_evidence.claim: Background on Bloch function theory; no specific resolution of the partial-sum growth problem with the positive-real-part hypothesis is indicated.
